tagline.text: Three linked islands, Gaspar, Melchor and Baltazar, in the sea south of Marinduque

location.label: Location
location.text: Off Barangay Pinggan, Gasan, Marinduque (about 30–45 minutes by boat from Gasan pier)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–2,500 (island hopping by boat and snacks; 2019 figures)

children.text: The Tres Reyes Islands are three islands off Gasan, Marinduque: Gaspar, Melchor and Baltazar. They are about 30 minutes by boat from Gasan pier, and only the largest, Gaspar, is inhabited, making them a known island-hopping destination for beaches, snorkeling and camping.

Tres Reyes means "Three Kings" in Spanish. The name refers to three islands named after the three Magi, Gaspar, Melchor and Baltazar, and they belong administratively to Barangay Pinggan in Gasan, Marinduque. They can be seen from the Gasan coast and take about 30–45 minutes by boat from Gasan pier. Wikipedia presents the islands as a potential tourist destination for Gasan, and Gaspar, the largest, is said to be the only inhabited one.

Marinduque is a heart-shaped island province in the sea south of Luzon. It became known first for the Moriones Festival held during Holy Week and for the old church in Boac, but travelers who want the sea head to the Tres Reyes Islands off Gasan. Cebu Pacific (Cebgo) has flown from Manila, and you can also take a boat to Balanacan Port from Batangas or Lucena. Gasan is about
16 km

from the provincial capital Boac, so it combines easily with a Boac-based itinerary. Gasan town itself has Guingona Park, where the Good Friday cenaculo is staged during Moriones, Reyes Park with its boardwalk, Talao Cave, a series of twelve caves, and Banot Beach Park, all described on Wikipedia. Gasan is the second-oldest town in Marinduque after Boac, and has local events such as the Gasang-Gasang Festival and Araw ng Gasan, the town founding day. A good plan is to make island hopping a one-day outing and spend another day or two around Gasan and Boac.

The appeal of the islands is their simplicity, without big facilities. Gaspar has a beach, huts and a camping area, while the other two are places to enjoy small sandy stretches and clear water. The most common way is to rent a bangka (traditional Philippine boat) at Gasan pier and tour all three islands, and 2019 sources list the three-island hop at

When planning, think first about travel time and weather. From Manila the flight to Marinduque Airport takes about
1 hour

, but flights have at times operated only on certain days, and going by land and sea takes a day. When the sea is rough, boats from Gasan pier may not sail. So when you add these islands to an itinerary, it is safest to prepare backup plans such as the Moriones Festival or sightseeing in Boac.

The largest of the three and the only inhabited one. Boats usually land on its beach, which is said to have huts, a camping area and simple food. Trips to Gaspar alone are quoted at a lower price, which also reflects that this island is the center of the visit.
An island with a small sandy beach where you can stop briefly during hopping to swim and take photos. There is almost no infrastructure, so bring drinking water and a trash bag.
Another small island on the hopping route. Reviews describe it as quiet with clear water, but conditions depend on weather and tides.
You can rent a mask and snorkel locally or bring your own. There are shallow areas with fish and coral, but ask your boatman about specific spots and check the currents.

blocks.title: Islands seen from the Gasan coast

children.text: The three islands are visible from the Gasan coast and pier. You can also see the boardwalk park (Reyes Park) and Guingona Park, the venue of the Holy Week Moriones events. By Wikipedia's account, Gasan is the second-oldest town in Marinduque.
Camping lets you watch the sunset and night sky over the sea with little light pollution. Camping depends heavily on weather and waves, so leave slack in your schedule.
Negotiate a bangka at Gasan pier and set off. Agree on the price, the number of people and the return time beforehand.
Arrive at Gaspar Island, look around the beach and hut area, and check water and food.
Stop at Melchor Island and Baltazar Island in turn to swim and snorkel.
Return to Gaspar for lunch and a rest.
Head back to Gasan. Set the return time before the wind picks up.
Boats are rented per boat, so the more people in your group, the lower the cost per person.
Take a boat from Gasan to Gaspar, get permission to camp and choose a tent spot.
Spend the time swimming and snorkeling.
Watch the sunset and have dinner.
Walk the morning beach, pack up and return to Gasan.
Flights have operated from Manila to Marinduque Airport (in Masiga, Gasan). A 2019 source listed Cebu Pacific flights from Manila on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, with round trips around
. Service changes often, so check when you book.
The airport is close to Gasan town. From the airport to the pier you can use a local tricycle or van; check fares locally.
Flights have been suspended and resumed more than once, so check the latest information.

Marinduque has a tropical climate without a sharply defined dry season, but February to May is generally calmer and clearer for island hopping. During Holy Week (Moriones Festival), crowds fill lodging and boats early, so arrange ahead.
From June to November rain is frequent and waves are high, so hopping boats often do not sail. In this period keep your schedule flexible and prepare sightseeing in Boac and Gasan as a fallback.

The earlier you set off in the morning, the calmer the sea and the gentler the light for photos and snorkeling. Winds can strengthen in the afternoon, so plan to return early, and the day before ask your lodging or people at the pier about tomorrow's sea conditions. Even on a sunny day, boats may not leave if the waves are high.

Overnight stays on the islands mean huts and camping on Gaspar; if you want a comfortable bed, lodging in Gasan, Boac or Torrijos is better. Beach Club Cagpo and Villa Briones in Torrijos are listed in sources, but check rates and condition.
The islands have almost no restaurants, so bring snacks, water and a trash bag. Buy a packed lunch or fruit in Gasan town. Reviews often mention bringing plenty of cash and a power bank.

Most travelers to Marinduque base themselves in Boac or Gasan and do island hopping as a day trip. To camp overnight you need a tent, sleeping bag, insect repellent and a flashlight, and if waves rise your return may be delayed, so keep a spare day. Sunscreen and a waterproof bag are worth preparing in advance.
Look for a boat the day before through the pier or your lodging.
Gaspar is often cash only, so bring plenty of cash.
Bring drinking water and snacks and carry all your trash back out.
You can rent or bring snorkeling gear; always wear a life jacket.
Ask local residents or the caretaker for permission before pitching a tent.
Agree on the return time with the boatman so you get back before sunset.
Use a hat and sunscreen that is gentle on coral.
Boat service and fares change with the weather, so check the latest information.
Even if the sea looks fine, winds often rise in the afternoon, so leave early in the morning and return in the early afternoon.
Agreeing with the boatman beforehand on the order of islands and how long to stay on each avoids price disputes later.
If the sea is rough, hopping boats may not sail or the return may be delayed. Do not push it on high-wave days.
You travel in small bangkas, so wear a life jacket and keep your luggage in a waterproof bag.
There is almost no medical facility or shop on the islands, so bring basic medicine and water.
Prices come from 2019 sources and may differ now, so confirm before negotiating.
Do not step on or touch coral, and leave no trash.
During Holy Week, boats and lodging can sell out because of the crowds.
Boat departures from Gasan pier depend on weather decisions, so do not schedule a tight same-day flight or ferry connection.
The island province that holds the Tres Reyes Islands, known for the old church in Boac and the Moriones Festival. Gasan is about
16 km
from Boac.
The provincial capital, with an old church, museum and town scenery. It is a good half-day before or after island hopping.
Marinduque's best-known beach, in Torrijos, with a view of Mount Malindig. Reach it from Gasan by jeepney or car.
The Reyes Park boardwalk in Gasan town and Talao Cave, a series of twelve caves, are listed in sources. Check locally whether the caves are open before visiting.
